abstract: Maintains records on diagnostic assay validation, sample turnaround velocity, and laboratory processing capacity
system_message:
You are the State Plant Pathology Lead (PATH). Your primary responsibility is maintaining records on diagnostic assay validation, sample turnaround velocity, and laboratory processing capacity for biosecurity surveillance protocols.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains records on diagnostic assay validation, sample turnaround velocity, and laboratory processing capacity（DIAG）
information_points.content:
PATH-DIAG-PIO：For the Mobile robotic automated qPCR sampling protocol, molecular assay validation clearance is confirmed (true) by the state diagnostic laboratory assay registry for target pathogen molecular marker panels. Laboratory tracking logs document an average field sample turnaround time of 24 h from field intake to result release, while equipment calibration records reflect a gross daily analytical capacity of 420 samples/day over two standard shifts.
PATH-DIAG-PXX：For the Autonomous multispectral drone survey protocol, molecular assay validation clearance is confirmed (true) under state diagnostic laboratory assay registry standards for target plant pathogen panels. Laboratory tracking logs show an average field sample turnaround time of 48 h from intake to result release, and equipment throughput records indicate a gross daily analytical capacity of 500 samples/day across two standard daily shifts.
PATH-DIAG-8W7：For the Canine olfactory scent detection protocol, molecular assay validation clearance is confirmed (true) according to the state diagnostic laboratory assay registry for target plant pathogen molecular marker panels. Additionally, laboratory tracking logs indicate an average field sample turnaround time of 24 h from sample intake to result release, and equipment throughput calibrations establish a gross daily analytical capacity of 420 samples/day across two standard daily shifts.

information_points.title: Pathogen genomic sequencing（GENOM）
information_points.content:
PATH-GENOM-QPR：For the Canine olfactory scent detection protocol, next-generation sequencing run logs for biweekly reference genome re-sequencing runs document a sequencing read depth of 30 X across target polymorphic loci.
PATH-GENOM-1EJ：For the Autonomous multispectral drone survey protocol, next-generation sequencing run logs for biweekly reference genome re-sequencing runs indicate a sequencing read depth of 50 X across target polymorphic loci.
PATH-GENOM-2LJ：For the Mobile robotic automated qPCR sampling protocol, next-generation sequencing run logs for biweekly reference genome re-sequencing runs record a sequencing read depth of 100 X across target polymorphic loci.
